industry.why: Neutral at industry level because it is split, carried. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): financials and real estate investment trusts were the only sectors bought in the week (Jefferies desk, 17 Oct), Wood favours financials as the diversification from artificial intelligence, and Goldman (16 Oct) says Southern European banks are healthier than in 2011-15; against it, French spreads at decade highs with new spillover to Italy, the sovereign-bank loop. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: C now, B prior. Banks C and Insurance B carry the view; Alternative finance D.

sector.why: Overweight, carried, with its tripwire re-tested and a reason not to go to Double Overweight. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): higher yields raise reinvestment income, the cases are large, simple and cash-yielding, and Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) is 'highly constructive into 2027' on Nordic property and casualty, where premiums have never fallen in twenty years and Gjensidige's sell-off misreads a strong result. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior, agrees. Not A, because this week's credit widening is exactly this row's counter-case: a second multi-sigma sell-off in credit excess returns and euro high yield 90 basis points wider since September, and asset books break first if the crack becomes a default cycle; the tripwire (a default cycle, not widening alone) has not fired. One Pool name (ASR Nederland, 30th on the starting score). To A if credit stabilises with the Nordic premium read repeated; to C on the first reported default wave.

geography.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): the Swiss index is among those Goldman (19 Oct) names as rallying alongside non-AI and low-beta exposures, which is the rotation this row was set on; the Swiss National Bank was not re-read this week, so last week's 'not hiking' stands. Relative strength is not graded by country. Counter-case unchanged: the franc takes 2 to 3 points a year off a Swiss exporter's reported profit (Sonova memo), and five of the Swiss Pool names are semiconductor names inside an Underweight sector. Back to C if the SNB joins the hikers or the franc reverses.
